html:
The khaen is a mouth organ made of bamboo pipes with metal reeds, the national instrument of Laos. It is played to accompany lam, the sung poetry of the Lao people.

Players can sustain chords and melody at once by breathing in and out. Lam singers trade improvised verses about love, faith or daily life, and the khaen drives the music at festivals, temple fairs and weddings.

In 2017 UNESCO listed khaen music of the Lao people as intangible heritage. The same music thrives in Isan, Thailand, where it grew into the popular mor lam style; see the Lao in Isan. Compare sticky rice, another shared mark of Lao culture, and Lan Xang.
